entries.heading: A payload you push, then drop
entries.text: OP_DROP carries data inside a Taproot leaf script. The payload is pushed onto the stack as an ordinary data push and the next opcode, OP_DROP, removes it again.

entries.heading: The mechanism
entries.text: A leaf script pushes five fields and runs OP_DROP after each of the first four. What is left is a public key and a signature check, so the leaf spends like an ordinary key path.

entries.heading: The stack, step by step
entries.text: The witness supplies the signature first, then the leaf script runs. The payload occupies the stack for exactly one opcode before OP_DROP removes it.

entries.heading: Why build another carrier
entries.text: OP_DROP puts the payload in the witness for the discount, inside code that executes, with no conditional branch anywhere in the script.

entries.heading: Two layers, one name
entries.text: The carrier layer fixes the leaf script grammar and is selected by 6269703131302d6f702d64726f70. The ledger layer fixes what the JSON means and is identified by p equals op-drop.

entries.heading: Bitcoin Universe surfaces
entries.text: Inscribe workspace, Core explorer, Core portfolio, and a feature-gated Core marketplace. Nothing outside Bitcoin Universe reads OP_DROP.

entries.heading: Scope and layering
entries.text: Rules OD-1.1 to OD-1.5. The carrier layer and the ledger layer are separate. A leaf can parse correctly and still change no balance.

entries.heading: Transaction anatomy
entries.text: Rules OD-3.1 to OD-3.6. Exactly three witness items, a 33-byte control block, a P2TR previous output, and output index 0 as the anchor.

entries.heading: Leaf script grammar
entries.text: Rules OD-4.1 to OD-4.9. Ten elements: marker, content type, digest, payload, public key, each followed by OP_DROP except the last which is OP_CHECKSIG.

entries.heading: Taproot commitment proof
entries.text: Rules OD-5.1 to OD-5.4. Leaf version 0xc0, Merkle root from the control block, key parity, and the output key must match the spent output.

entries.heading: Payload encoding
entries.text: Rules OD-6.1 to OD-6.13. Compact UTF-8 JSON, string values only, fixed key order, four-character tick, positive integer strings with no leading zero.

entries.heading: Identifiers
entries.text: Rules OD-7.1 to OD-7.5. A reveal event id is txid colon i vin colon w1. A settlement event id is txid colon s vin colon the transfer event id.

entries.heading: Operations
entries.text: Rules OD-8.1 to OD-8.7. Deploy, mint, and transfer. First valid deploy wins. Credited equals the smaller of the requested amount and the remaining supply.

entries.heading: Deterministic ordering
entries.text: Rules OD-9.1 to OD-9.4. Block height, then transaction index, then operation index. Settlements apply before reveal leaves inside a transaction.

entries.heading: State transitions
entries.text: Rules OD-10.1 to OD-10.8. Available and reserved balances, the two-stage transfer, settlement to output 0, and the return path when no destination exists.

entries.heading: Invalid conditions
entries.text: Every reason code and the exact condition that produces it: invalid_taproot_commitment, invalid_anchor, ambiguous_transfer_anchor, missing_transfer_source_authorization, invalid_transfer_destination, unsupported_profile, unsupported_self_mint, duplicate_deploy, unknown_tick, mint_limit_exceeded, supply_exhausted, insufficient_available_balance.

entries.heading: Optional media attachment
entries.text: Rules OD-12.1 to OD-12.6. A deploy may append a drops-media image up to 256 KiB, chunked at 256 bytes, each chunk followed by OP_DROP.

entries.heading: Conformance
entries.text: Rules OD-13.1 to OD-13.4. An implementation conforms when it reaches the same decision, reason code, and balances as the test vectors.

entries.heading: Where the bytes live
entries.text: OP_RETURN puts data in an output script at four weight units per byte. Witness envelopes and OP_DROP put it in the witness at one. Stamps puts it in the UTXO set.

entries.heading: Property matrix
entries.text: Data location, weight per byte, transactions needed, UTXO set impact, prunability, payload size, whether data executes, and ecosystem tooling.

entries.heading: Cost, worked out
entries.text: The same 54-byte payload priced four ways. OP_RETURN about 165 vB in one transaction, OP_DROP about 315 vB across two, an envelope about 310 vB, Stamps about 230 vB plus permanent UTXO cost.

entries.heading: Against OP_RETURN
entries.text: OP_RETURN is provably unspendable so it never enters the UTXO set. It is the better choice for a small payload in one transaction.

entries.heading: Against witness envelopes
entries.text: The Ordinals-style envelope wraps content in OP_FALSE OP_IF and OP_ENDIF so it is skipped. OP_DROP executes the push and the drop and uses no conditional opcode.

entries.heading: Against Stamps unprunable outputs
entries.text: Stamps stores data in outputs that stay in the UTXO set, giving the strongest retention at the highest externalised cost.

entries.heading: Where OP_DROP is worse
entries.text: No external tooling, roughly twice the cost of an OP_RETURN for a small payload, it adds a UTXO, 256-byte pushes, invisible until the reveal, and a narrower ledger profile than the carrier.

entries.heading: Three operations
entries.text: Deploy defines a token, mint requests units under existing rules, transfer moves units you already hold in two confirmed steps.

entries.heading: Worked example: a mint, end to end
entries.text: Minting 1000 drop: the 54-byte event, the 158-byte leaf, the commit address, the reveal witness, and the result.

entries.heading: Worked example: a transfer
entries.text: Moving 250 units: reserve on the reveal, then settle by spending the anchor. Output 0 of the settling transaction is the destination.

entries.heading: Reading a result
entries.text: Pending, warming up, valid, transfer_pending, settled, invalid with a reason, and no token found: what each one means and what to do.

entries.heading: The $DROP token
entries.text: $DROP is the display label for wire ticker drop. Maximum supply 21,000,000, limit 1,000 per mint, 21,000 full-limit mints, no decimals.

entries.heading: Support matrix
entries.text: Inscribe workspace wired for deploy, mint, and transfer. Core portfolio wired. Core explorer feature-gated behind opDropIndex and Core marketplace behind opDropTrading, both off by default. Selling unsupported. No third-party support.

entries.heading: Staying in control
entries.text: Never enter a seed phrase, read the exact JSON before approving, check output ordering for a transfer, and treat pending as not a balance.

entries.heading: Terminology
entries.text: Carrier marker, protocol identifier, leaf script, control block, anchor, owner, available, reserved, transferable, total, event id, minted, remaining, holder.

entries.heading: Indexer semantics
entries.text: Confirmation depth is per deployment, the mainnet floor is one confirmation and the reference configuration uses six. A single writer scans, replicas serve committed state.

entries.heading: Mempool
entries.text: The ledger never includes mempool. Provisional tracking reports mempool, mined, or finalized and never affects balances.

entries.heading: Reorg behaviour
entries.text: Automatic recovery is bounded: 24 blocks by default, up to 144, and 100,000 rebuilt rows. Deeper divergence needs an authenticated operator replay.

entries.heading: Fee and size
entries.text: Reveal sizes: deploy 164 vB, mint 160 vB, transfer 160 vB. Weight is base bytes times four plus two plus witness bytes. Budget for the commit transaction as well.

entries.heading: Standardness and relay
entries.text: An OP_DROP transaction is an ordinary Taproot script-path spend. No special policy applies, standard weight and dust limits do, and relay is per node.

entries.heading: Limitations
entries.text: One event per leaf, 256 bytes per push, four-character tickers, no decimals, no self-mint, output 0 sensitivity, one transfer per transaction, no third-party support.

entries.heading: Security considerations
entries.text: The payload is permanent and public, the key in the leaf must be yours, output 0 discipline matters, anchor control is settlement control, and deploys can be front-run.

entries.heading: Implementation checklist
entries.text: Separate checklists for an encoder, a decoder, and an indexer, each testable against the test vectors.

entries.heading: Valid leaves
entries.text: V1 deploy drop, V2 mint 1000, V3 transfer 250, V4 the largest possible deploy payload, each with script hex, digest, commit address, and control block.

entries.heading: Commitment vectors
entries.text: T1 to T6: valid commitment, wrong previous output, non-P2TR previous output, wrong leaf version, a 65-byte control block, and a four-item witness.

entries.heading: Invalid leaves
entries.text: I1 non-minimal push, I2 unknown marker, I3 digest mismatch, I4 reordered keys, I5 whitespace, I6 five-character ticker, I7 a conditional opcode, I8 carrier valid but ledger invalid.

entries.heading: Ledger sequences
entries.text: Supply arithmetic including the partial final mint: a request of 30 against a remaining supply of 10 is valid and credits 10.

entries.heading: Transfer sequences
entries.text: X1 a transfer that settles, X2 a transfer that returns because output 0 yields no address, X3 rejected transfers including ambiguous anchors.

entries.heading: Service boundary
entries.text: The indexer owns confirmed-chain scanning and ledger state. Browsers must never call it directly; a first-party backend holds the origin.

entries.heading: Endpoints
entries.text: GET /op-drop/health, /op-drop/launch/drop, /op-drop/tokens, /op-drop/tokens/{tick}, /op-drop/balances/{address}, /op-drop/events, /op-drop/indexer/status.

entries.heading: Response schemas
entries.text: Deployment, balances, event, and indexer status field by field. Amounts are always decimal strings, never JSON numbers.

entries.heading: Consuming safely
entries.text: Keep the origin server-side, treat amounts as strings, check freshness, handle reversal, and verify what matters against block data.

entries.heading: Decoder
entries.text: Paste a leaf script hex to see the pushed payload, the decoded fields, the stack evolution step by step, and the reveal size.

entries.heading: Builder
entries.text: Choose an operation and a ticker, supply an x-only key, and get the exact leaf script hex with its digest and fee estimate.

entries.heading: What these tools do not check
entries.text: The Taproot commitment, ledger state, the anchor and settlement, and the media attachment are all outside the reach of a leaf-only tool.

entries.heading: Specification 1.0.0
entries.text: First numbered publication of the specification, 2026-09-01. No wire format change: every previously valid leaf is still valid.

entries.heading: Versioning policy
entries.text: Major means a validity or balance change, minor means an ignorable optional capability, patch means clarification. There is no version field in the payload.
